purpose: Attribution of the installed D package CPU under the CPU40 load; descriptive single run, not a comparative gain or acceptance

package.note: Installed signed package D; ASCII guard candidate not included

command: scripts/cp5-d-measure.py --scenario stream1 --visibility visible --renderer coregraphics --warmup 5 --duration 45 --sample-every 5; after 20 s: sample <app> 12 and sample <fixture> 12
sampler: macOS sample, 12 s; 8067 main-thread samples (about 1.49 ms interval). Busy = samples whose leaf is not a blocking wait.

fixture.topOfStack: Swift String building (String(repeating:count:), _StringGuts.append, __CFStringAppendFormatCore, malloc/free); write() 333 samples
fixture.conclusion: Fixture CPU is mostly its own user-space string formatting, not PTY kernel time

conclusions: Rendering, not parsing, dominates app CPU: per-frame NSAttributedString and CTLine construction for every visible row plus CG rasterization is about 18 of roughly 27 app CPU points in this run.
At 1 MiB/s the whole visible grid is new on every frame, so a row cache alone cannot remove this cost; a direct glyph path for simple cell runs is required.
The engine feed (about 1.5 points) and the PTY read path are minor; the per-read 16 KiB zeroed allocation plus Data copy is a small fixed cost.
limits: Single run, sampler overhead included; shares are attribution, not acceptance numbers.
Metal renderer not profiled in this run.
Real provider TUIs redraw far fewer rows per frame; this load is the worst-case scroll path.
